# NTK Viewer Progress

컨텍스트 압축 후에는 이 파일을 먼저 읽고 이어간다. 앞으로 작업 기록은 `NTK_VIEWER_PROGRESS.md`에 누적한다. 이전 임시 기록 파일 `NTK_ACK_WORKLOG.md`의 내용은 이 파일로 흡수한다.

## Active Goal

NTK 모드에서 랜덤 만화/웹툰 뷰어 성능 안정성을 개선하고 검증한다. 현재 최우선은 ACK 정상성이다. ACK가 정상화된 뒤 이미지 즉시 표시, 스크롤 프레임 안정성, 스크롤 위치 유지, 랜덤 테스트 자동화/병렬화를 계속 진행한다.

## Non-Negotiable Rules

- ACK 성공은 실제 `/api/ad/ack` 200 응답과 `ntk_server_ack_success_recorded`, `ntk_ack_proof`, 또는 동등한 strict proof가 있어야만 성공으로 판단한다.
- `acked=true`만으로 성공 처리하지 않는다.
- 뷰어를 늦게 여는 방식, 웜업으로만 속도 올리기, 타이머/딜레이/눈속임 보정, 테스트 조건 완화, 실패 케이스 제외, 특정 작품/회차 하드코딩은 금지한다.
- 사용 디바이스는 `emulator-5556`이다. `emulator-5554`는 쓰지 않는다.
- 의미 있는 개선 단위가 검증된 뒤에만 커밋/푸시한다.
- 새로 발견한 사실, 수정, 테스트 결과, 다음 액션은 이 파일에 계속 추가한다.

## Current Main File

- `app/src/main/java/ml/melun/mangaview/mangaview/NtkWebViewFallbackManager.java`

## Applied Changes

- Versioned guard resource path 처리:
  - `/wasm/ad-guard/ad_guard.js?v=...` -> `/api/ad/guard-js?v=...`
  - `/wasm/ad-guard/ad_guard_bg.wasm?v=...` -> `/api/ad/guard-wasm?v=...`
  - `NtkQuicBridge.request(apiUrl, "GET", headersJson, "")` 사용
  - 200이 아니면 stale versioned bundled asset fallback 하지 않음
  - `localGuardModuleResponse(url)`는 versioned guard URL에 null 반환
- Guard module bridge/cache 수정:
  - `NtkQuicBridge.request()`에서 `cachedGuardModuleResponse(url)`와 stripped/decoded guard response 적용
  - guard GET timeout 2600ms
  - `requestGetBatch()`는 guard response를 기억하고 source `cached_guard` 사용
- Guard JS WebView patch:
  - `stripEncryptedGuardLoader`가 `patchGuardLoaderForWebView` 호출
  - `WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming` 문자열을 `__ntkNoInstantiateStreaming`으로 변경
- Strict proof gating:
  - `markAck()`는 기존 proof를 덮지 않음
  - `markProofAck(source,tp)` 추가
  - ACK-only에서 `acked=function(){return ackProofed();}`로 strict화
  - `bridgeReq`에서 `/api/ad/ack` POST 200 + ok/acked/status ok면 `markProofAck('direct-bridge-ack-200', tp)` 호출
- Native bridge proof wrapper 추가:
  - JS에서 `NtkQuicBridge.request`를 래핑
  - `/api/ad/ack` POST 200 + ok/acked/status ok면 `markProofAck('native-bridge-ack-200', rq.tp)` 호출
  - 설치 로그: `ackProofNativeBridgeInstalled`
- ACK readiness gate 복구:
  - bridge 존재만으로 ACK script를 시작하지 않도록 변경
  - `else if(!readyComplete && !ackBridgeReady)` -> `else if(!readyComplete)`
  - runtime loading wait도 `ackBridgeReady`로 우회하지 않게 변경

## Current Problem

`/api/ad/ack` 200과 `ntk_server_ack_success_recorded`는 안정적으로 재현되지만, JS strict proof 상태가 true로 바뀌지 않는다. `ackProofNativeBridgeInstalled`는 찍히지만 `ackProofNativeBridge` 또는 `ntk_ack_proof`가 찍히지 않는다. 따라서 active `installGuardBeaconBridge`가 `NtkQuicBridge.request` 래퍼를 우회하거나, 래퍼 설치 후 다른 wrapper가 다시 덮어쓰는 순서 문제가 유력하다.

## 2026-06-14 Scroll Frame-Pacing Probe

- 원인 분리:
  - `ReaderSurfaceView`는 `View.onDraw()` 기반이며 `surface_jank_v3`의 missed frame은 draw 시간이 아니라 onDraw callback/post 사이 간격으로 계산된다.
  - `drawState()`의 실제 렌더링 시간은 random runs에서 계속 1ms 미만이다.
  - `assertNoSchedulerGap=false`이므로 현재 harness 실패 기준은 dropped/total draw 쪽이고, callback/post missed frame은 참고 slowSignal이다. 다만 UX 목표상 계속 분리한다.
- 실험:
  - fling 중 `scheduleFrameLocked(preferImmediate = pointerDown || dragging)`를 `preferImmediate = true`로 바꿔 continuation invalidation을 더 aggressive하게 예약했다.
  - 빌드 성공 후 `/webtoon/17332/1515337`, seed `1781416807331`, strict fresh target, native-ack, `ScrollSteps=2`로 검증했다.
  - run dir: `build\ntk-random-perf\20260614_150342`.
- 결과:
  - script passed, failures=0, ACK assertion 통과.
  - ACK: `ntk_webview_ack_preflight_done success=true,ms=11547`, strict proof `native-fetch-ack-200`.
  - 이미지/위치: 두 scroll step 모두 `missingPx=0`, `placeholderPx=0`, postStopDrift delta 0.
  - slowSignals는 2개 그대로 남았다.
  - callback/post P95는 약 140ms로 개선되지 않았다.
  - draw/total은 낮지만 기존보다 소폭 증가했다(`drawP95=0.11~0.12ms`, `totalP95=0.30~0.55ms`).
- 결정:
  - fling continuation을 무조건 immediate invalidation으로 바꾸는 접근은 효과가 없어 되돌렸다.
  - 이 slowSignal은 현재 render work 자체보다 test touch injection, UiAutomation/device timing, emulator frame delivery, 또는 frame stats active window가 quiet/settle 구간을 포함하는 방식에서 비롯될 가능성이 높다.
  - 기준 완화는 하지 않는다. 다음은 계측 window를 더 정확히 분리해 실제 fling 중 callback gap과 settle 이후 gap을 따로 기록하는 방향이 적절하다.

## 2026-06-14 ACK Bridge Phase Probe and Signed-Bridge Fix

- phase 계측 probe: `build\ntk-random-perf\20260614_151815`
  - 대상: `/webtoon/17332/1515337`, seed `1781416807331`, strict fresh target.
  - 결과: script passed, ACK assertion 통과.
  - 그러나 `ntk_webview_ack_preflight_done success=true,ms=20652`로 악화됐다.
  - phase 로그로 병목을 분리했다:
    - `/api/ad/challenge`: network 665ms, cookies 591ms, total 1260ms.
    - `/api/ad/canary`: network 342ms, cookies 1451ms, total 1802ms.
    - 이후 canary flush는 최대 cookies 2347ms까지 관찰됐다.
  - 원인: ACK-only ad-control POST마다 `CookieManager.flush()`가 반복되어 0.7~2.3초의 동기 지연을 만든다.
- 수정 1:
  - `applyWebViewCookies(url, result, flush)` overload를 추가했다.
  - ACK ad-control bridge 경로(`/api/ad/challenge`, `/api/ad/canary`, `/api/ad/ack`)에서는 WebView in-memory cookie 적용과 app jar sync는 유지하되, 디스크 `CookieManager.flush()`는 생략한다.
  - `submitCanaryBeforeAdAck()`의 canary 적용도 flush 없이 처리한다.
- 검증: `build\ntk-random-perf\20260614_151937`
  - 결과: script passed, ACK assertion 통과.
  - phase 개선:
    - challenge/canary `cookiesMs`가 1~3ms로 감소.
    - ad-control POST total은 대체로 317~340ms 수준으로 감소.
  - 하지만 ACK preflight는 `20382ms`로 여전히 나빴다.
  - 원인: native `fetch('/api/ad/ack')` signed path가 `400 missing_canary`를 반복했고, missing-canary fast retry가 새 challenge를 계속 만들었다.
- 수정 2:
  - ACK-only `installGuardBeaconBridge()` 이후 guard가 `/api/ad/ack` POST를 호출할 때 native fetch를 우선하지 않고 Java bridge signed ACK를 우선하도록 wrapper를 추가했다.
  - wrapper는 현재 ACK body를 signer로 서명한 뒤 `NtkQuicBridge.request('/api/ad/ack')`로 직접 전송한다.
  - Java bridge는 canary-before-ack, scoped `ad_ack_c`, `ad_guard_l`, app cookie merge를 관리하고, 실제 200 응답에서만 `markProofAck('guard-fetch-ack-200')`를 호출한다.
- 검증: `build\ntk-random-perf\20260614_152155`
  - 결과: script passed, failures=0, ACK assertion 통과.
  - firstDrawable 1697ms.
  - `guardBridgeSignedAckPreferredStart keyId=...` 후 `/api/ad/ack` bridge phase:
    - `ntk_viewer_ad_bridge_canary_before_ack ... code=200,ms=294`.
    - `/api/ad/ack` `networkMs=626,cookiesMs=1,totalMs=631`.
    - `guardBridgeSignedAckPreferred status=200`.
    - strict proof: `ntk_ack_proof source=guard-fetch-ack-200`.
    - `ntk_webview_ack_preflight_done success=true,ms=8371`.
  - 이미지/위치: 2개 scroll step 모두 `missingPx=0`, `placeholderPx=0`, `loading=0`, `errors=0`, postStopDrift delta 0.
  - `missing_canary`는 이 target run에서 사라졌다.
- 비교:
  - same target baseline `20260614_150342`: preflight 11547ms + first drawable 후 1800ms quiet.
  - bridge gate/450ms quiet `20260614_151229`: preflight 11045ms.
  - flush 제거만 `20260614_151937`: phase는 개선됐지만 native signed ACK missing-canary 반복으로 preflight 20382ms.
  - bridge-preferred signed ACK `20260614_152155`: preflight 8371ms, strict proof 유지, missing-canary 없음.
- 판단:
  - `CookieManager.flush()` 반복 제거는 ad-control bridge phase의 확실한 병목 제거다.
  - native signed ACK보다 Java bridge signed ACK 우선 경로가 현재 ACK 안정성과 속도 모두에 유리하다.

## 2026-06-14 ACK Transport Retry + Promote Guard Rechecks

## 2026-06-14 Fix Candidate: Defer Full Episode WebView Fetch Until First Bitmap

- 원인 정리:
  - 통과 run `20260614_185204`는 first drawable 전 episode fetch가 `DIRECT_ONLY`로만 관측됐다.
  - 실패 run `20260614_185325`는 early URLs 설치 직전/직후 `ALLOW_SHARED_WEBVIEW` episode fetch가 Cloudflare 응답을 만나 hidden WebView fallback을 시작했다.
  - 그 직후 `/api/ad/challenge` bridge와 HTTP2 retry timeout이 first drawable 전에 실행됐고, page0 decode ready 뒤 `reader_anchor_delivery_queue_delay page=0,ms=2691`가 발생했다.
- 구현 후보:
  - `ReaderSession.kt`
  - NTK early URLs가 이미 설치되면 현재 initial full fetch task와 cancellation group을 취소한다.
  - 첫 bitmap이 실제로 전달되거나 first-frame 예산 구간이 지나기 전까지 full episode fetch/WebView fallback을 재시작하지 않는다.
  - 첫 bitmap 이후에는 새 background cancellation으로 full fetch를 다시 실행하고 기존 `appendInitialNtkUrlsAfterEarlyInstall()` 경로로 전체 이미지 목록을 붙인다.
- 의도:
  - viewer open을 늦추는 것이 아니라, 이미 확보한 early image path의 첫 bitmap delivery가 WebView/ACK fallback에 밀리지 않게 우선순위를 분리한다.
  - strict ACK 200 proof 경로는 제거하지 않는다. 첫 drawable 이후 기존 deferred ACK/WebView preflight가 계속 실행되어야 한다.
- 다음 검증:
  - build/install.
  - target repro `/webtoon/17332/1515337`, seed `1781430403208`.
  - 같은 target 3-run, `/manhwa/25694/1768331` 3-run, broader random strict fresh.

## 2026-06-14 Additional Validation: Unknown Count Tail Trim Is Unsafe

- `/manhwa/34074/1709547` target run `20260614_201110`:
  - result:
    - failed with visible loading `1`.
    - firstDrawable `2260ms`.
    - frame stats collected but showed callback stalls:

    - ACK strict proof was false because the test failed before ACK completion; do not treat as ACK success.
  - important structural finding:
    - full generated parse reported `images=44`.
    - later p018 generated request hit png timeout plus jpg 404.
    - `ReaderImageCache` treated unknown image count and `page >= 18` as likely past tail.
    - `ReaderSession.trimNtkGeneratedTail` accepted `Generated image past tail` with `knownCount=0`.
    - result:
      - `trim_generated_tail start=17,count=27,known=0,total=17`.
      - visible scroll then operated on only 17 pages, not the 44 parsed pages.
  - 판단:
    - single generated image failure must not delete the rest of a random episode.
    - tail trim must require a reliable count; unknown-count page-number heuristics are unsafe for strict random.
  - action:

## 2026-06-15 ACK Root Cause Follow-up: Hardblock Was Preserving Stale Clearance

- comparison:
  - success `20260615_012016`:
    - `ntk_native_ack_prepare_challenge_code=200` at attempt 0.
    - ACK WebView cookie summary already had `adAckC=true`.
    - delay 2500 probe saw real episode shell with title and `init-html-sentinel`.
    - `/api/ad/challenge` 200 then `/api/ad/ack` 200.
  - failure `20260615_023101`:
    - native prepare challenge was CF `403` on all attempts.
    - logs showed `ntk_native_ack_hardblock_preserve_clearance ... proof=false,recent=false,fresh=true`.
    - ACK WebView then kept `cf_clearance=true` but stayed on Cloudflare `Enable JavaScript and cookies to continue` / `Performing security verification`.
    - `adAckC=false` throughout, so `/api/ad/challenge` and `/api/ad/ack` both returned CF `403`.
- generic root cause:
  - existing hardblock policy preserved a fresh-looking `cf_clearance` even when there was no recent verified NTK access.
  - for ACK this can be stale: cookie exists, but server still sends CF challenge and never produces the episode shell/sentinel that seeds `ad_ack_c`.
- applied follow-up:
  - on NTK ACK hardblock, if there is no recent verified access, clear native CF cookies and WebView CF cookies even if the saved clearance looks fresh.
  - log marker: `ntk_native_ack_hardblock_stale_clearance_reset`.
  - this is a generic stale-clearance recovery; it does not relax ACK proof.
- next validation:
  - rebuild.
  - rerun strict fresh target.
  - expected: ACK-only WebView starts a fresh CF flow instead of reusing stale clearance; success still requires real `/api/ad/ack` 200.

## 2026-06-15 Generic ACK Ordering Fix: Do Not Wait Through Initial CF

- user concern:
  - fixes must be generic, not one failed episode at a time.
  - ACK success already proved in `20260615_012016`; current task is to preserve that success structure across fresh/random states.
- comparison:
  - successful run had initial CF probes all `cf=false`, then native `/api/ad/challenge` returned `200`, WebView cookie summary had `adAckC=true`, and bridge `/api/ad/ack` recorded real `200`.
  - failing runs show early direct/RSC/page fetches marking Cloudflare before reader ACK preflight starts; native challenge then returns `403` and hardblock cache is set before WebView can get `adAckC`.
- generic root cause:
  - reader defers ACK until first drawable for normal image speed, but when initial CF appears this delay lets page/image recovery traffic harden the Cloudflare state.
  - this is a state-machine ordering bug, not a target-specific image or episode bug.
- applied change:
  - added `CustomHttpClient.prepareNtkNativeAckChallengeForViewer(baseUrl, path)`.
  - `ReaderV2Activity` now starts this lightweight native challenge prepare immediately after reader window setup and before `manga.startNtkVerifiedInitialImageProbe(...)`.
  - initial CF probe now starts deferred ACK preflight immediately on `cf=true` instead of waiting for early images/first drawable.
- constraints preserved:
  - no viewer-open delay.
  - no ACK proof relaxation.
  - strict success still requires real `/api/ad/ack` 200 and `ntk_server_ack_success_recorded`.
- validation next:
  - rebuild.
  - rerun strict fresh target `/webtoon/17332/1515337` seed `1781432391654`.
  - expected improvement: `ntk_native_ack_prepare_viewer_start` appears before page/image hardblock traffic; if the challenge returns 200, `adAckC=true` should appear before WebView bridge ACK.

  - Good run `20260615_012016`: first drawable logged at `16:20:28.750`; ACK preflight started later at `16:20:29.652` with reason `first_drawable_ready`; native challenge returned 200 and seeded `adAckC=true`.
  - Failing run `20260615_032521`: initial CF probes 1-4 were false, probe 5 became true; ACK preflight started at `18:25:29.851` with reason `initial_continuous`, the same millisecond as first drawable; native challenge immediately returned 403 and hardblock was cached.
- generic root cause:
  - `initial_continuous` could start ACK before `firstDrawableMetricLogged` was set, bypassing the intended post-first-drawable quiet window.
  - This is not specific to `/webtoon/17332/1515337`; any random episode whose initial pages become continuous just before first drawable could hit the same race.
- applied change:
  - `ReaderV2Activity.maybeStartDeferredNtkAckAfterInitialContinuous()` now waits for first drawable before it can start ACK.
  - If initial continuous is ready first, it logs `reader_ntk_ack_preflight_wait_first_drawable reason=initial_continuous` and schedules another quiet check instead of starting native/WebView ACK immediately.
- constraints:
  - Does not delay opening the viewer.
  - Does not relax ACK proof; strict success still requires real `/api/ad/ack` 200 and `ntk_server_ack_success_recorded`.
  - No target/seed hardcoding.
- validation next:
  - rebuild.
  - rerun strict fresh `/webtoon/17332/1515337` seed `1781432391654`.
  - required first check: ACK start should no longer happen at the same ms as first drawable due to `initial_continuous`.

## 2026-06-15 Generic RSC Launch-Hold Gate: Move Protection to CustomHttpClient

- user reminder:
  - New failures must not be handled as one-off seed fixes.

- generic root cause:
  - Reordering `Manga.java` call sites helps only the visible parser path.
  - Other concurrent fetch paths can still call `mgetNtkViewerPayloadPage(...)` directly before first drawable and put the NTK session into Cloudflare 403 before ACK has a clean chance.
  - Therefore the protection belongs at the shared HTTP/RSC entry point, not at one parser branch.

  - While the per-episode launch hold is active, RSC payload fetch is skipped and cached page fallback is returned.
  - New marker: `ntk_rsc_payload_skip_launch_hold path=...`.
- intended effect:
  - First drawable can be served by generated/cached image candidates without letting any early RSC/direct payload request create CF hardblock state.
  - This is generic across NTK `/webtoon/` and `/manhwa/` launch flows because all RSC payload fetch callers pass through `CustomHttpClient`.
- validation next:

  - rerun strict fresh target `/webtoon/17332/1515337` seed `1781432391654`.
  - required:
    - `ntk_rsc_payload_skip_launch_hold` before first drawable.

    - first drawable and scroll coverage still pass.
    - strict ACK success still requires real `/api/ad/ack` 200 and `ntk_server_ack_success_recorded`.

  - guard-created /api/ad/ack body reaches native bridge instead of failing at decode.
  - strict ACK remains gated on real /api/ad/ack 200.

## 2026-06-15 21:08:00 +09:00 ACK flow comparison: successful UX keeps CF document alive; hidden episode path ends early

- Compared:
  - Successful normal UX/`EnsureAccessBefore` run: `build\ntk-random-perf\20260615_080908`.
  - Failed hidden episode probe run: `build\ntk-random-perf\20260615_082423`.
- Successful visible `CaptchaActivity` sequence:
  - Initial Turnstile probes return `{"type":"none"}` for roughly the first 1-2 seconds.
  - The real challenge-platform / Turnstile iframe appears later:
    - Turnstile iframe detected around `23:09:13.429`.
    - Touch sequence completes around `23:09:13.519`, then repeats around `23:09:17` and `23:09:20`.
  - `cf_clearance` appears around `23:09:21.130`.
  - Normal page/access cookies then appear in order:
    - `ntk_fp`, `ntk_pid`, `newtoki_recent`, `newtoki_read`, `__vsid`, `__ntk_ev_id`, `__ntk_et_id`.
  - `/api/ad/canary` then creates `ntk_blk_ok_sig` and `ad_ack_c`.
  - `ad_guard_l` appears, then `/api/ad/ack` posts with a real `challengeToken`, `requestKeyId`, and observation URLs.
  - Native ACK proof later sees real `/api/ad/challenge`, `/api/ad/canary`, and `/api/ad/ack` `200`.
- Failed hidden episode sequence:
  - Direct RSC returns Cloudflare `403`.
  - Hidden pre-ACK `/api/ad/challenge {"path":...}` returns Cloudflare HTML `403` with `cookieLen=0`.
  - Hidden WebView navigates episode URL and gets main-frame `403`.
  - Only one Turnstile probe ran at `650ms` and returned `{"type":"none"}`.
  - Around `0.8s` after episode navigation, hidden document extraction produced blocked HTML and `finishOnMain(..., reset=true)` ended the task:
    - `ntk_viewer_parse reason=blocked ... code=0 ... images=0`
  - Later probe windows never happened because the task had already completed/reset.
- Code-level difference:
  - `CaptchaActivity` does not finish on main-frame HTTP 403. It keeps WebView resource loading, console observation, cookie polling, normal-page probes, and Turnstile clicking active.
  - `NtkWebViewFallbackManager.onBridgeResult(...)` immediately finishes navigated documents when `isBlockedNtkDocumentBody(body)` is true:
    - `finishOnMain(task, code > 0 && code != 200 ? code : 403, body, true);`
- Important caution:
  - A prior bad experiment proved simply extending hidden wait to 12s is harmful.
  - Therefore the next fix must not be "wait longer and hope"; it must preserve/drive the actual challenge lifecycle or route to the real `CaptchaActivity` access flow without pretending ACK is complete.
- New candidate direction:
  - Determine the minimal generic condition that lets the challenge DOM continue to Turnstile iframe/`cf_clearance`:
    - do not prematurely extract/finish blocked challenge HTML,
    - mirror `CaptchaActivity` resource-triggered probing only while a real challenge document is active,
    - keep hard fail bounded and explicitly marked as captcha when no clearance/challenge progress appears.
  - If this still cannot finish before viewer budget, treat it as an access-acquisition limitation and keep strict ACK false rather than hiding it.

- Bad assumption to avoid:
  - Do not interpret "ACK 200 happened" as image API readiness if no request key was recorded/attached.
  - Do not treat `EnsureAccessBefore` with only `hasNtkAccessProof()` as a fully normal UX baseline.
- Change under test:
  - In the ACK-only bridge path, just before posting `/api/ad/ack`, if `window.__ntk_request_key_id` is missing, retry request-key registration once with a bounded `1600ms` wait.
  - This does not delay opening the viewer and does not relax ACK proof.
  - If the retry succeeds, the same request key can be injected into ACK body and attached to the native image API.
- Rejection criteria:
  - Revert or revise if the retry delays ACK materially without producing `ntk_request_key_recorded`, or if ACK 200 still lacks `requestKeyId` and image API remains 403.

  - In `20260615_095216`, first API CDN image stream started and joined correctly, but `image-full` won after being submitted with the normal stagger.
  - Current normal race staggers attempts by `FOREGROUND_RACE_DELAY_MS=120ms`.
  - For the first image from early `/api/webtoon-images`, delaying either full or foreground lane can directly affect first drawable budget.
- Code change:
  - `ReaderImageCache.requestForegroundRace` now detects whether the requested image equals the first URL stored in `earlyNtkImageUrls(manga.ntkEpisodePath)`.
  - Only for that first early API image, all foreground race attempts use `delayMs=0` and `image-full` is placed first.
- Why this is not a forbidden shortcut:

  - It does not accept ad/board images.
- Risk:
  - Slightly more simultaneous network work for the first image only.
  - If foreground transport is consistently faster on some hosts, full-first ordering could regress; validation must catch this.

## 2026-06-15 operating rule update: record bad approaches as first-class history

- User correction:
  - Bad/failed approaches must be recorded in this file, not only successful changes.
  - The reason is operational: after context compaction or heartbeat resume, the next worker must know what not to retry.
- Rule:
  - Every failed experiment, regression, weak proof, fake success path, or abandoned shortcut must be appended with:
    - what was tried
    - exact run/log evidence when available
    - why it failed or why it is unsafe
    - whether it was reverted, retained only as diagnostic code, or still under observation
    - explicit "do not retry" guidance if applicable
- Current negative lessons to keep prominent:
  - Do not chase one failing episode with hardcoded fixes. Any fix must generalize across random NTK manga/webtoon episodes.
  - Do not declare ACK success unless strict `/api/ad/ack` 200, request-key proof, and `/api/webtoon-images` success are all present.
  - Do not treat advertising/board/upload images as valid viewer pages. Host trust alone is insufficient; path/content class filtering is required.
  - Do not spend more time only reordering first-image foreground races until the earlier ACK/API/URL handoff delay is measured and reduced.
  - Do not repeat earlier plain-CF promotion timing probes, blind guard-image wait reductions, delayed viewer-open tactics, cache-only wins, or loading/delay masking.
- Next workflow:
  - Before each new experiment, check this section and the "bad experiment" sections above.
  - If a new idea resembles a rejected approach, add instrumentation first or change the underlying proof condition; do not retest the same shortcut with a different timeout.

## 2026-06-15 experiment in progress: use strict WebView ACK preflight from viewer launch path

- Finding:
  - Product `Utils` launch path already starts an NTK ACK preflight immediately before `startActivity`.
  - That preflight was native-only (`performNtkNativeAckBypass`), while current reliable strict proof for modern guard is WebView ACK preflight.
  - The direct stress test constructs `ReaderV2Activity` intent directly, so it did not use the product launch preflight path and logged `nativeStarted=false`.
- Code change:
  - Rename/expose `Utils.startNtkViewerAckPreflightForLaunch(...)`.
  - Launch preflight now tries `performNtkWebViewAckPreflight(path)` first, then falls back to native bypass only if WebView strict proof fails.
  - `NtkRandomStressInstrumentedTest.viewerIntent(...)` calls the same launch helper and sets `viewerNtkAckPreflightStarted` when it starts.
- Why this is acceptable:
  - The preflight starts at viewer launch time, not as a separate cache warmup before launch.
  - It does not delay opening the viewer and does not fake ACK success.
  - Success still requires strict `/api/ad/ack` proof, request-key, and image API success.
- Risk:
  - If WebView launch preflight competes with the Reader image API preflight, it may add contention instead of reducing latency.
  - Validation must compare ACK timing and first drawable; if it regresses, record and revert.

## 2026-06-15 bad experiment: launch-path WebView ACK preflight caused ACK contention and severe regression

- Change tested:
  - Product launch preflight and direct stress-test intent started `performNtkWebViewAckPreflight(path)` at viewer launch, falling back to native ACK on WebView failure.
  - This was intended to overlap strict ACK proof with Activity startup without delaying viewer open.
- Validation:
  - Full build/install strict fresh focused run.
  - `build\ntk-random-perf\20260615_101608`
  - Command:
    - `.\tools\ntk_random_perf.ps1 -DeviceSerial emulator-5556 -Runs 1 -ScrollSteps 4 -AppendSteps 0 -ScreenshotEvery 0 -Seed 1781469172752 -Mode native-ack -ScrollInputMode touch -ScrollPattern mixed -HoldAfterFirstDrawableMs 1000 -TargetEpisodePath /webtoon/849277/nv-849277-2 -StrictFresh -NoAppendProbe -ForceStopBeforeRun -EnsureAccessBefore -EnsureAccessMaxMs 30000`
- Result:
  - Failed first drawable badly: `11913ms` > `3500ms`.
  - Pipeline summary lost image API timing because the viewer never reached normal first-drawable flow in budget.
  - ACK phases:
    - first WebView launch preflight: `ack_only_fetch=537/558`, then `viewer_ntk_ack_preflight_webview_done success=false`.
    - fallback/native ACK and bridge ACK returned `code=400`.
    - Reader-side WebView preflight then stalled: `ack_only_fetch=12709/12714`.
  - Log evidence:
    - `ntk_native_ack_control_single_done ... code=400`
    - `ntk_native_ack_bridge_submit code=400`
    - `ntk_viewer_ad_bridge_response ... code=400 ... {"ok":false,"error":"missing_canary"}`
    - `ntk_request_key_recorded ... source=ad-ack-request`
    - second `ntk_webview_ack_preflight_stage ... ack_only_fetch,ms=12709,totalMs=12714`
- Diagnosis:
  - Starting a full WebView ACK preflight at launch races the Reader-owned ACK/image API path.
  - On failure it also triggers fallback native ACK too early, with incomplete canary state, producing `missing_canary`.
  - This is not a general performance win; it contaminates ACK state and can create a long second ACK-only fetch.
- Action:
  - Reverted the launch-path WebView preflight experiment immediately.
  - Restored product launch preflight to native-only.

  - JS bridge read `getNativeAckChallenge` at `01:44:30.511` and got `bytes=0`.
  - Native challenge was recorded at `01:44:30.515`, only about 4ms later.
  - Because the JS missed the native challenge cache by a few ms, it fell back to browser/bridge `/api/ad/challenge` and added about `505ms` before `directAckProofFirstFast3Challenge`.
- Code change:
  - Add a bounded wait in `ViewerImageBridge.getNativeAckChallenge(...)` for ACK-only proof calls.
  - It polls up to `160ms` for the already-started native challenge producer to record its result.
  - This is not a fake wait for UX; it fixes a producer/consumer race and should avoid a much slower duplicate `/api/ad/challenge` fallback when the native challenge is effectively ready.
- Risk:
  - If native challenge preparation is genuinely absent or slow, this can add up to `160ms` before fallback.
  - In the current ACK-only preflight path, native challenge preparation is always started before the ACK script, so the expected behavior is to catch near-miss races like `20260615_104424`.

  - `Manga`: direct text extraction no longer accepts raw `board_uploads` URLs unless the document also has explicit board page markup (`vw-imgs`/`alt="page "` or an `images[{page,src}]` style payload). `webtoon_uploads`, `manhwa_uploads`, and `comic_uploads` remain allowed.

## 2026-06-15 code action: separate urgent visible decode gate

- Change:
  - Added a dedicated `urgentVisibleDecodeGate` in `ReaderSession` with bounded parallelism `3`.
  - `requestPage(...)` now uses this gate for `visiblePriority` decode work instead of sharing the busy gate.
- Reason:
  - Focused failures show actual visible rows can stay behind initial continuous warm/recovery work.
  - The previous structure used `urgentNetwork`/`urgentDecode` executors but still acquired `busyDecodeGate` when the viewport was busy, so visible promotion could be blocked by non-visible busy work.
- Scope:
  - This is not a global startup expansion and does not add hardcoded title/episode/page behavior.
  - The gate is bounded to avoid repeating the failed broad-contention experiments.
- Validation required:
  - Build debug + androidTest.
  - Rerun focused strict fresh repro for `/manhwa/19859/293953` seed `1781491642531`.
  - Success requires strict ACK `/api/ad/ack` 200 plus no visible placeholder/loading and improved frame stats.

## 2026-06-15 code action: visible generated byte hedge

- Change:
  - Added `visibleGeneratedByteHedges` in `ReaderSession`.
  - When an actual visible NTK generated page starts or is skipped because an old active urgent load already exists, schedule a bounded one-shot foreground byte fetch on `urgentNetwork`.
  - The hedge calls `prefetchImageFile(..., foreground = true)` but does not directly deliver or duplicate decode.
- Reason:
  - In `20260615_132435`, p010/p011 visible requests happened several seconds before their generated-direct foreground fetch actually started.
  - Reissuing full decode requests was already tried and worsened contention, so this only pulls bytes/cache forward for visible generated pages.
- Safety constraints:
  - Only after first bitmap.
  - Only NTK generated page refs.
  - One hedge per page until page set refresh/cancel.
  - No scroll position correction, no delay, no test relaxation, no hardcoded episode/page.
- Validation required:
  - Build.
  - Focused strict fresh repro.
  - Check whether p010/p011 `foreground_race_generated_direct_start/done` and `visible_generated_byte_hedge_done` occur earlier and whether placeholder coverage improves.

## 2026-06-15 code action: foreground generated fetch gate bounded bypass

- Change:
  - Added `NTK_GENERATED_FOREGROUND_GATE_BYPASS_AFTER_MS = 180`.
  - In `ReaderImageCache.withNtkGeneratedFetchPermit(...)`, foreground generated p004+ requests now try to acquire the foreground generated gate for 180ms.

  - This may increase concurrent foreground generated requests. If it causes socket resets or worse frame/placeholder metrics, revert and record as bad.
- Validation required:
  - Build.
  - Focused strict fresh repro.
  - Confirm p010/p011 direct start no longer waits multiple seconds for the gate.

## 2026-06-15 code action: visible generated foreground supersedes background flight

- Change under test:
  - Track whether an image cache flight was started as foreground-capable.
  - If a generated image has an active background flight and a later visible foreground request arrives, cancel/supersede the background flight and start the foreground path instead of joining the background timeout.
- Reason:
  - In `20260615_135403`, `p012` was requested by visible foreground but logged `flight_join foreground=true activeFlight=true`, then the underlying result was `foreground=false` background QUIC timeout.
  - This means final viewport images can inherit slow/background behavior from earlier prefetch, which is a structural priority inversion.
- Safety:
  - Applies only to generated images when a visible foreground-capable request arrives over a non-foreground active flight.
  - No hardcoded page/title/episode and no test relaxation.
- Validation required:
  - Build.
  - Focused strict fresh repro seed `1781491642531`, path `/manhwa/19859/293953`.
  - Check for `flight_supersede_background_generated` and whether loading/placeholder drops without breaking ACK 200.
- Bad/weak risk to watch:
  - If canceling background flights causes too much churn or loses useful bytes, revert this specific supersede logic.

## 2026-06-15 code action: add focused perf retry wrapper for inconclusive runs

- Problem:

- Safety:
  - Same seed/path/mode/test conditions are reused.
  - Real image coverage, ACK, first drawable, and scroll assertion failures remain failures.
  - Inconclusive retries are recorded in the wrapper output and can be traced to each generated summary directory.
- Validation required:

  - Use wrapper for the next focused strict fresh repro to reduce manual rerun overhead.

## 2026-06-15 finding: p001 first drawable priority inversion behind initial recovery

- Evidence:
  - Focused run `20260615_141157` failed before scroll: first drawable `8142ms`.
  - Timeline showed p001 foreground stream failed early, then `generated_original_retry_skip_active_recovery` aborted the actual foreground retry while an initial recovery flight was active.
  - The protected recovery flight later timed out/failed, and only a later retry delivered bytes quickly; the final network/decode was fast but arrived too late.
- Root cause candidate:
  - In `ReaderImageCache.fetchForegroundBytes`, actual foreground display fetch calls `requestWithNtkGeneratedFallback(... skipInitialForegroundGeneratedRetryOnActiveFlight = useForegroundTransport)`.
  - For first generated pages, this can make the user-visible foreground path yield to an already active recovery/prefetch flight.
  - This is a priority inversion: a recovery task can block the path that would put the current viewport image on screen.
- Code action under test:
  - Let the actual foreground stream retry continue even when an initial recovery flight is active.
  - Keep this narrow to foreground display fetch behavior; do not add delay, loading screen, fixed warmup, or test relaxation.
- Risk to watch:
  - Extra foreground retry could increase network contention. If first drawable or ACK proof worsens, revert this change and record it as a bad approach.

## 2026-06-15 run 20260615_145747/145914/150041/150340: no draw samples are caused by unloaded visible pages, not invalidate failure

- Validation:

  - `onDraw` does run after programmatic scroll, but `buildDrawStateLocked()` returns null.
  - Logged state: `shouldDraw=true`, `renderRequested=true`, `defer=false`, `pages=35`, but state is null.
  - Root condition in code: after a content frame has already been drawn, `buildDrawStateLocked()` refuses to draw a state with no drawable content: `hasDrawnContentFrame && !state.hasDrawableContent`.
  - That means the viewport after scroll contains only unloaded pages, and the renderer correctly avoids replacing the current frame with a blank placeholder-only frame.
  - Programmatic scroll initially did not dispatch a new window request; fixed by making `testScrollByPixels()` dispatch `windowRequestLocked(true)` after changing `scrollOffset`.

  - `/api/m/i` fallback returned `image/gif len=42` with signature `GIF89a 1x1`, which is not a real manga image and must never be accepted/displayed.
- Code actions under test:
  - `ReaderImageCache.looksLikeImage()` now rejects tiny GIF responses and only accepts GIFs with reasonable byte length and dimensions.
  - `ReaderImageCache.isUsableImage()` now rejects cached page images smaller than `64x64`, preventing 1x1 pixel/ad/tracking images from becoming page content.
  - Removed the foreground-only skip in `retryNtkGeneratedAfterNativeAck()`, so visible foreground images can use native ACK recovery after generated direct fetch failures. Launch first-draw hold still blocks ACK recovery before first drawable.
- Bad/weak approach to avoid:
  - Do not solve `frameStats=null` by fabricating a jank sample. The real issue is that no drawable page exists at the scrolled viewport.
  - Do not accept any GIF by signature alone. Tiny 1x1 GIF responses are not manga content.
  - Do not skip native ACK recovery just because an image is foreground/visible; visible failures need the strongest recovery path after first drawable.

## 2026-06-15 current fix under test: visible generated recovery must use strict bridge ACK proof, not empty native tp

- User correction:
  - Bad or misleading approaches must stay in this MD so the same weak strategy is not retried after context compression.
  - Recent successful ACK proof existed in this MD and in logs; current 428 failures do not mean ACK is impossible.
- Success/failure comparison:
  - Successful run `build\ntk-random-perf\20260615_145611` reached real strict ACK:
    - `ntk_viewer_ad_bridge_native_submit code=200`
    - `ntk_server_ack_success_recorded ... source=bridge-ack-200`
    - `guardBridgeSignedAckPreferred ... status=200 ... requestKeyId=true`
    - `ackChecks.strictProof=true`
  - Failing run `build\ntk-random-perf\20260615_152243` did not reach that bridge proof before visible image recovery:
    - image recovery called native ACK while WebView ACK was in flight and got `ntk_native_ack_skip_existing_inflight ... webview=true`.
    - an earlier native ACK attempt submitted empty `tp` and received `428 {"ok":false,"error":"ad_proof_required"}`.
- Finding:
  - The proven path is WebView/bridge signed ACK with request key/proof, not the native empty-`tp` bypass.
  - Empty-`tp` native ACK is harmful for visible image recovery because it can create proof-required state without producing a usable strict proof.
  - WebView ACK in-flight should be treated as a proof source to join, not as a reason to immediately fail visible image recovery.
- Code action under test:
  - Added `CustomHttpClient.waitForNtkWebViewAckPreflightProof(path, timeoutMs)` to bounded-wait for existing WebView/bridge strict proof/cookie.
  - Changed `ReaderImageCache.retryNtkGeneratedAfterNativeAck()` so foreground generated-image recovery:
    - first accepts existing usable ACK proof/cookie,
    - joins an in-flight WebView ACK proof for a bounded time,
    - starts the proven `performNtkWebViewAckPreflight(path)` path when no proof flight exists,
    - then retries the image only if strict ACK proof is available.
  - The recovery path no longer starts the empty-`tp` native ACK bypass for foreground generated image failures.
- Validation plan:
  - Rebuild and rerun the focused strict-fresh programmatic repro for `/manhwa/19859/293953`, seed `1781491642531`.
  - Required evidence:
    - no new `ntk_native_ack_ack_code=428 ... ad_proof_required` from visible generated recovery,
    - `generated_native_ack_retry_join_webview` or `generated_native_ack_retry_start_webview`,
    - strict proof log such as `ntk_viewer_ad_bridge_native_submit code=200` or `ntk_server_ack_success_recorded`,
    - p002/p003 become drawable and `placeholderPx` drops from the previous `723`.
- Bad/weak approach to avoid:
  - Do not use native empty-`tp` ACK as the primary visible generated-image recovery mechanism.
  - Do not treat WebView ACK in-flight as a simple failure. Join it briefly for strict proof/cookie.
  - Do not weaken ACK success criteria; only real `/api/ad/ack` 200/proof is success.

- Expected effect:

  - ACK strict proof remains a separate requirement and still must be measured after first drawable.

## 2026-06-16 02:25 Diagnosis: common state-machine gap, not infinite random cases

- User question:
  - "개선하고나면 왜 또 문제가 생기는거야? 케이스가 이렇게 다양할리가 없잖아"
- Answer:
  - The failures are not many unrelated random cases. They are different symptoms of the same NTK startup graph:
    - ACK proof / guard proof state
    - `imagesToken` / `imageMetas` extraction
    - `/api/*-images` signed image API
    - runtime `/api/m/i` image URL discovery in WebView
    - generated URL extension (`jpg` vs `jpeg`)
    - first-page stream/decode/draw publish
  - Point fixes expose the next gate because these lanes currently compete and cache failures independently.
- Current concrete bad state:
  - `CustomHttpClient.fetchNtkViewerImageUrls(...)` returns early for modern numeric generated episodes with:
    - `ntk_images_api_skip_modern_numeric_generated_direct`
    - `cacheNtkViewerImageUrlMiss(cacheKey)`
  - This prevents the later `fetchNtkViewerImageUrlsUncached(...)` path from checking WebView runtime cache or trying the bounded modern numeric image API lane.
  - It can also poison the same episode with `ntk_images_api_miss_cache_hit`, even though WebView may later intercept real `/api/m/i` image URLs.
- Patch direction:
  - Remove the early skip/miss-cache for modern numeric generated episodes.
  - Let the existing uncached method handle modern numeric episodes; it already:
    - checks cached WebView image URLs first,
    - tries bounded pre-ACK image API,
    - returns without caching a miss on modern numeric pre-ACK miss.
- Why this is broader than retry-order patches:
  - It does not prioritize one episode or extension.
  - It removes a shared false-negative cache gate so all generated numeric NTK episodes can reuse real runtime/API image evidence when available.
- Validation pending:
  - Build and fixed replay seed `1781541134619`, path `/manhwa/35212/1761599`.

## 2026-06-16 02:39 Patch: break initial structure-publish / first-bitmap circular wait

- Root cause found in `build\ntk-random-perf\20260616_015813`:
  - `foregroundRaceWin p001.jpeg ms=1644`
  - `foregroundStreamDone ms=1923`
  - `decodeReady ms=4783`
  - `reader_anchor_delivery_queue_delay page=0,pagesReady=false`
  - `early_urls_append_full_publish_deadline firstBitmap=false ms=19891`
  - `reader_open_to_first_drawable ms=21798`
- Meaning:
  - The image bytes and decode were ready much earlier than visible draw.
  - `appendInitialNtkUrlsAfterEarlyInstall(...)` began a structure publish and intentionally waited for first bitmap before publishing the full generated list.
  - The anchor bitmap delivery then hit `isStructurePublishPending()` and was queued again before `logFirstBitmapIfNeeded(...)` could run.
  - This created a circular wait:
    - full publish waits for `firstBitmapLogged`
    - first bitmap delivery waits for structure publish to finish
    - publish only finishes at deadline
- Patch:
  - `shouldDeliverInitialGeneratedDuringStructurePublish(...)` now allows the initial anchor page through while `firstBitmapLogged` is still false.
- Why this is broad:
  - It applies to any NTK source where first decoded anchor is blocked by an initial structure publish.
  - It does not change test budgets, delay viewer opening, or hardcode an episode.

## 2026-06-16 23:13 HTML fallback ad-image guard

- User concern carried forward:
  - "이미지에 광고이미지 절대 안 섞이게."
- Root risk found:
  - `ReaderImageCache.replaceWithImageExtractedFromHtml()` can recover from an HTML response by extracting `<img>` candidates.
  - The existing filter rejected obvious chrome such as `logo`, `sprite`, `favicon`, `thumb`, and non-NTK hosts, but it did not explicitly reject ad/banner/popup path segments before page images.
  - If an HTML fallback page puts an ad/banner image before the true page image, that candidate could waste recovery attempts and, in loose URL shapes, risk becoming the replacement image.
- Fix applied:
  - Added `isLikelyAdChromeImageCandidate()` to reject URL path segments and filenames such as:
    - `/data/banner/`, `/banner/`, `/banners/`
    - `/advert/`, `/advertise/`, `/advertisement/`, `/ads/`
    - `/popup/`, `/popups/`
    - `/sponsor/`, `/promotion/`, `/promotions/`
    - filename prefixes `ad_`, `ad-`, `banner_`, `banner-`, `popup_`, `popup-`
  - Kept the filter segment/prefix based so random hash fragments containing letters like `ad` are not rejected accidentally.
- Test added:
  - `ReaderImageCacheInstrumentedTest.ntkHtmlFallbackRejectsAdChromeImagesBeforePageImages`
  - Verifies that ad/banner candidates before a valid `webtoon_uploads/page001.jpg` are ignored and only the page image remains.
- Validation:
  - Build:
    - `./gradlew.bat :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest` passed.
  - Focused instrumentation:
    - `adb -s emulator-5556 shell am instrument -w -r -e class ml.melun.mangaview.reader.ReaderImageCacheInstrumentedTest ml.melun.mangaview.test/androidx.test.runner.AndroidJUnitRunner`
    - Passed: `OK (3 tests)`.
  - Short viewer regression:
    - `./tools/ntk_random_perf.ps1 -DeviceSerial emulator-5556 -Runs 3 -ScrollSteps 8 -AppendSteps 0 -ScreenshotEvery 0 -Seed 1781568409738 -Mode native-ack -ScrollInputMode programmatic -ScrollPattern mixed -HoldAfterFirstDrawableMs 1800 -StrictFresh -NoAppendProbe -NoAckAssert -ForceStopBeforeRun -SkipBuild -SkipInstall`
    - Result: `build/ntk-random-perf/20260616_111004`
    - `passed=True`, first drawable `3/3`, scroll `24/24`, slow signals `0`, failures `0`.
    - Limitation remains: `curated-only`; live root/API discovery is still blocked.
- Bad/avoid:
  - Do not solve ad-image mixing only by visual inspection after load.
  - The safer invariant is to prevent ad/chrome candidates from entering the HTML fallback replacement list in the first place.

## 2026-06-17 00:42 ACK empty POST contamination fix

- Latest failing strict run inspected:
  - `build/ntk-ack-ux-probe/20260616_120715_sbxh7_com_95a6d8`
  - Probe ended with `ack=false,clearance=true,serverProof=false`.
  - The page reached the real episode, but `/api/ad/ack` responses were repeatedly observed as HTTP 400.
- Comparison with the successful strict proof run:
  - Success run: `build/ntk-ack-ux-probe/20260616_115647_sbxh7_com_156c47`
  - It had a single site/WebView ACK POST followed by:
    - `ntk_server_ack_success_recorded path=/webtoon/17332/1515337,source=captcha-webview-ack-200`
    - `NTK WebView ACK proof recorded status=200`
- Root cause isolated:
  - The app/test rearm path was directly firing `fetch('/api/ad/ack',{method:'POST',credentials:'include',cache:'no-store'})`.
  - That sends an empty or incomplete ACK payload and caused repeated HTTP 400 responses.
  - Normal strict success requires the site's guard logic to generate the ACK request/body.
- Fix applied in working tree:
  - Removed direct empty `/api/ad/ack` POST from:
    - `CaptchaActivity.scheduleNtkAdAckRearmAfterLocalGuard`
    - `CaptchaActivity.waitForNtkAdAckAndFinish`
    - `NtkCaptchaLiveInstrumentedTest.triggerAckRearm`
  - Kept `ntk-ack-rearm` event dispatch so page-side guard logic can react if it has a real handler.
  - Throttled `__NTK_BRIDGE_FETCH_READY__` console logging to one line per page to avoid log noise.
  - Hardened `tools/ntk_ack_ux_probe.ps1`: strict ACK mode now throws if `serverProof` is missing.
- Bad/avoid:
  - Do not synthesize `/api/ad/ack` POST with an empty body. It produces 400 loops and can prevent or obscure the real site ACK.
  - Do not accept `probeDone` or cookie-only `ad_ack_c` as strict success when `serverProof` is empty.

## 2026-06-17 13:42 p001 anchor slow-stream fix attempt

- Failure being targeted:

  - Do not fix p001 by waiting longer for the active foreground stream. It delays fallback when p001 is slow.
- Code-level cause found:
  - In `ReaderImageCache.getOrFetch()`, when foreground stream wait timed out, `priorityFullDownload=true` was set but `downloadAtomically(... foreground=false)` was still used.
  - That meant the recovery full download got permit priority but bypassed foreground race/range-first behavior.
- Current fix:
  - Reverted the join timeout to `900ms`.
  - Changed timeout-recovery generated full download so `priorityFullDownload` is passed as a foreground request to `downloadAtomically`.
  - This should make p001 timeout fallback use the existing foreground/range/direct race path instead of a slow background-style request.

## 2026-06-17 p001 anchor join budget split

- Sparse-hole failure build/ntk-random-perf/20260616_152720: p001 unowned foreground stream started from Manga.java at about 0.36s after open with page=-1/permit=null. ReaderSession joined it, waited 650ms, then started a priority range/full cache flight; first drawable missed by ~187ms (3687ms).

  - Do not let stale stored NTK roots outrank the build's current canonical root unless a trusted resolver explicitly points there.

## 2026-06-18 22:45:00 +09:00 Emulator-only: strict ACK 200 race after captcha/clearance

- Artifact:
  - `build/ntk-random-perf/20260617_221337`
- Repro:
  - Seed `1781701774416`
  - path `/manhwa/8209/63505`
- Result:
  - First drawable timed out because ACK preflight stalled:
    - `webViewAckPreflightDone success=false ms=58511`
  - Captcha/Cloudflare itself was not the blocker:
    - `cf_clearance` appeared.
    - document verification was `code=200`.
    - `ad_ack_c` was present and scoped.
  - Strict `/api/ad/ack` was the blocker:
    - early/native bridge submit returned `400` or `428`.
    - No final `ntk_viewer_ad_bridge_native_submit code=200` in this artifact.
- Root cause:
  - There is a race between challenge/canary/impression/proof and the strict ACK POST.
  - Some code paths recorded `native-challenge-ad-ack-cookie-200` / challenge cookie as server ACK success even though it was not strict `/api/ad/ack` 200.
  - Native ACK fallback attempted canary after a failed ACK but had only one loop attempt, so it did not retry the actual ACK after canary became OK.
  - The ack-only JS fast path could enter `guardAck(ch)` before the ordered proof/canary/ACK sequence, creating a long false path.
- Patch applied, pending validation:
  - Native ACK fallback retry loop expanded from 1 to 3 attempts so canary fallback can be followed by a real ACK retry.
  - Added an ack-only `Fast4` JS override that orders strict ACK as: challenge -> impressions -> proof -> canary -> `/api/ad/ack`, with one immediate canary retry on `missing_canary`.
- Bad/avoid:
  - Do not count `ad_ack_c` or challenge 200 as successful ACK. Final proof must include strict `/api/ad/ack` 200.
  - Do not let hidden ack-only loop spin for ~58s after strict ACK failure; failed ordered ACK should retry quickly or fail fast with a clear reason.
  - Do not confuse document/page 200 with image API/ACK success.

  - Do not treat ACK 200 as enough. ACK can be correct while the reader still fails to install any image pages.
  - Do not let a verified/cached first image sit only in `ReaderImageCache` while the page list remains empty.
  - Do not fix this by raising first drawable timeouts; the right fix is to hand off verified early URLs while the full fetch is still in flight.
  - Do not base the initial NTK draw gate on mutable `currentPage` during first render; pre-draw/scroll movement can make the gate wait for non-visible pages.
  - Do not require manhwa page 2 for the initial gate when page 0/page 1 already cover the visible viewport.
- Fixes applied:
  - `ReaderSession.fetchInitialAllowingEarlyNtkUrls(...)` now keeps polling for late early URLs while the full initial fetch is still in flight, up to `NTK_EARLY_URL_LATE_HANDOFF_WAIT_MS=30000`.
  - When a late verified early URL appears, it installs immediately via `installEarlyNtkUrls(...)`, logs `early_urls_before_fetch_done_late`, and continues the full fetch in the background.
  - `ReaderV2Activity.isInitialContinuousScrollReady()` now evaluates the initial first-page gate from the original anchor page `0` while first drawable has not been logged, instead of the mutable `currentPage`.
  - Manhwa initial ready-ahead was reduced from 2 to 1 because page 0/page 1 cover the first visible viewport in tested manhwa cases, while waiting for page 2 caused unnecessary gate timeout.

- Real failure found in broader random strict fresh:
  - Artifact: `build/ntk-random-perf/20260618_130714`.
  - Seed: `1781755634161`.
  - Path: `/manhwa/35194/1762270`.
  - Title: `부인이 무서워서 큰일입니다`, episode `11화`.
  - imageEpisodeId `61100`, workId `35194`, imageCount `28`.
  - First drawable succeeded: `reader_open_to_first_drawable ... page=4 ms=3908`.
  - ACK succeeded: `/api/ad/ack` `200`, body `ok=true`, `seen=4`, strict `native-fetch-ack-200` proof recorded.
  - Failure: after fast-down scroll, visible viewport was all placeholders: `drawablePx=0 missingPx=0 placeholderPx=2274 loading=2 pages=28`.
  - Scroll position itself was stable: post-stop drift `maxPageDelta=0`, `maxOffsetDelta=0`.
- Diagnosis:
  - This is not captcha/Cloudflare/ACK. ACK is green before the visual failure.
  - Fast scroll lands around anchor/page 11. Visible generated image bytes are fetched (`foreground_race_win` for p009-p012), but visible pages can stay behind the original active loading/decode path and coverage is sampled before decode/delivery catches up.
  - Existing `visible_generated_byte_hedge` only fetched bytes. It did not force a visible cached decode after bytes were available, so `reader_visible_request_skip_active` could leave a visible placeholder dependent on the slower original in-flight decode.
- Fix:
  - `ReaderSession` now adds `visibleGeneratedDecodeHedges`.
  - After a visible generated byte hedge succeeds and the actual image file is cached, it enqueues an urgent cached decode/delivery for that still-visible page.
  - The original active fetch is not cancelled; duplicate decode delivery is naturally dropped by existing delivered/pending checks.
  - This is not timer masking: the extra path only runs after real bytes exist in cache.
  - Hedge state is cleared on cancel/structure reset/index shift.
- Target repro validation after fix:
  - Artifact: `build/ntk-random-perf/20260618_131210`.

  - Previous append publishes prepended pages immediately.
  - `ReaderSession.appendResolvedEpisode(... direction < 0)` shifts current page state forward and posts `onPagesPrepended(...)`.

  - The new previous episode pages were not decoded/delivered yet, so the viewport jumped from already drawable current pages into fresh placeholder pages.
  - This is a structure/publish timing bug, not an ACK proof bug.
- Fix:
  - `ReaderV2Activity.consumePrependedBoundaryReveal(...)` now defers automatic previous-boundary reveal for NTK readers.
  - Existing page/index preservation remains intact: `currentPage += insertedCount`, and `renderView.prependPageCount(..., reveal=false)` keeps the user's visible current content stable while previous pages warm in the background.
  - Log marker added: `pages_prepended_reveal_deferred_ntk inserted=...`.

## 2026-06-18 18:08:00 +09:00 prepend boundary placeholder narrowed without blocking append

- Fix:
  - Added a narrow `ReaderSurfaceView` render invariant for structure-change windows.
  - During `structuralScrollAdjustUntilMs`, if the first visible item is a newly exposed leading placeholder that is clipped at the top, covers only a small viewport fraction, and the next visible page already has drawable content, that placeholder fragment is skipped for the current draw frame.
  - This does not block append on network/decode, does not move the scroll offset, and does not hold the whole frame. It only prevents a top-edge prepended boundary sliver from becoming visible while its bitmap is still catching up.
- Why this is different from the reverted bad approach:
  - It does not synchronously decode new pages before `onPagesPrepended(...)`.
  - It keeps append publish fast, and relies on the next scheduled render to reveal the page when the bitmap arrives.

## 2026-06-18 18:57:00 +09:00 ACK defer starvation fixed on main

- Problem:
  - Broader strict fresh random found `/webtoon/11902/1483342` seed `1781775514871`.
  - The earlier hardblock path let WebView ACK start before first drawable; that overlapped the first scroll and caused severe callback jank.
  - Simply removing `allowBeforeFirstDrawable` avoided the overlap, but exposed a second bug: ACK never actually started after scroll. Logs showed repeated `ntk_webview_ack_preflight_join_proof_done ... inFlight=false` and `reader_ntk_ack_preflight_deferred_wait_quiet reason=quiet,quietMs=3500` until the 70s strict ACK assertion timed out.
  - Root cause was scheduler starvation:
    - `deferredNtkAckPreflightQuietRunnable` re-entered `maybeStartDeferredNtkAckAfterInitialContinuous()`, so post-quiet ACK could be blocked again by initial-continuous readiness after scroll.
    - `readerWindowBusy` could remain true if a busy=false window callback was not delivered after programmatic scroll. ACK quiet calculation then returned a fresh 3500ms delay forever.
- Fix:
  - `deferredNtkAckPreflightQuietRunnable` now calls `startDeferredNtkAckPreflight("quiet")` directly. The ACK start path still enforces first-drawable, strict floor, scroll quiet, and recovery hold checks, but it no longer loops back into initial image readiness.
  - Prepared native ACK failure/error no longer uses `allowBeforeFirstDrawable=true`; fallback WebView ACK must wait for first drawable and scroll quiet.
  - Initial Cloudflare/image-ready ACK block paths no longer force before-first-drawable WebView ACK.
  - ACK quiet calculation now releases stale `readerWindowBusy` for ACK scheduling once the last busy signal is older than `NTK_ACK_PREFLIGHT_SCROLL_QUIET_MS`, logging `reader_ntk_ack_preflight_stale_busy_released`.
- Validation:
  - Build passed: `./gradlew.bat --no-daemon :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest`.

    - First drawable was fast (`3750ms`), coverage had no missing/placeholder/loading, but ACK never started.

    - Scroll coverage: no visible loading, missing pixels, placeholder pixels, or scroll drift.
  - Live random validation:

    - Runs=2, strict fresh, clear ACK/cache, force-stop, live random required.
    - Result: OK (1 test), failures 0.

- Bad conclusion / bad approach to avoid:
  - Do not allow WebView ACK before first drawable just because native prepared challenge fails. It can overlap initial scroll and cause frame callback debt.

## 2026-06-18 19:28:00 +09:00 Captcha success-close ANR root cause

- Problem:
  - Wider strict fresh live-random `Runs=6` failed after 5 completed cases.
  - Artifact: `build/ntk-random-perf/20260618_190948`.
  - Completed cases had clean viewport coverage and strict ACK proof; this was not an image/scroll/ACK-200 failure for those cases.
  - Failure:
    - Instrumentation died with `Input dispatching timed out ... CaptchaActivity ... FocusEvent(hasFocus=false)`.
    - Captcha was opened from true-random API title selection after `Cloudflare challenge` on `https://sbxh8.com/api/manhwa-list?page=3276&pageSize=1&withTotal=1`.
    - `CaptchaActivity` resolved that API URL to `https://sbxh8.com/manhwa`, loaded the page, observed cookies with `adGuard=true,adAck=true`, posted `/api/ad/challenge`, verified document access `code=200`, and logged `finished with verified NTK clearance proof=false recent=true`.
    - Immediately after that, Activity pause/top-resumed state loss timeouts and a 7006ms HWUI frame appeared; the ANR happened while closing the already-successful captcha Activity.
  - Root cause:
    - `finishWithVerifiedClearance()` detached and synchronously destroyed the active WebView on the UI thread before calling `finish()`.
    - WebView renderer shutdown and window transition overlapped, blocking focus/lifecycle dispatch long enough for the system to flag `CaptchaActivity` as unresponsive.
- Fix in progress:
  - Successful NTK captcha close now detaches the WebView but schedules `destroy()` after the close transition instead of destroying synchronously.
  - Existing immediate destroy remains for ordinary `finish()` / `onDestroy()` paths that are not already using the verified-clearance success path.
- Bad conclusion / bad approach to avoid:
  - Do not count `Runs=6` as a pass just because ACK and scroll succeeded for the first 5 cases; instrumentation death is a real stability failure.
  - Do not blame this one on ACK 200. The completed cases had strict proof; the failure is captcha success-close lifecycle jank.
  - Do not fix by increasing instrumentation/ANR timeouts. The correct fix is removing heavy WebView destruction from the close transition.

- Continued on `C:\Users\Administrator\Downloads\mangaviewer-main-sync` `main`.
- Problem narrowed:
  - Slow strict ACK cases were not failing because images were blocked.
  - The proof-capable WebView path could install a signed ACK bridge wrapper and then send `/api/ad/ack` with an empty/request-key-only body before the real `challengeToken + tp` proof body existed.
  - Those invalid early posts produced repeated 400-style ACK attempts and delayed the eventual strict proof.
- Bad experiment rejected:
  - Temporarily enabled `nativeAckAugmentedBridge` for every augmented native fetch body.
  - Target repro passed but still took about `50.2s`, and logs showed unsigned full proof bridge posts returning `missing_challenge`.
  - Conclusion: unsigned augmented native bridge posts are not the right fast path; keep them disabled.
- Code change kept:

## 2026-06-19 00:15:00 +09:00 QUIC executor shutdown grace removes Cronet callback rejection noise

- Continued active goal on `main` after checking `NTK_VIEWER_PROGRESS.md`.
- CI status before code change:
  - GitHub Actions `Release APK` for `120b064ed` completed successfully: run `27768172223`.
- Root cause narrowed:
  - Actual UX recheck had 50 `cr_CronetUrlRequestContext RejectedExecutionException` lines.
  - These were concentrated around short-lived `HttpEngine` races and early/canceled requests.
  - `NtkQuicFetcher.fetchWithTransport(...)` and `Session.close()` shut down the callback executor immediately after `engine.shutdown()`. Android Cronet can still deliver late cancel/upload/read callbacks after the request result has already returned, so the terminated executor rejects those callbacks.
  - This did not break the visible fallback path, but it made ACK/image transport races noisier and less deterministic.
- Fix:
  - `NtkQuicFetcher` now shuts down the `HttpEngine` immediately but keeps the callback executor alive for a short 1500ms grace period via a daemon scheduled closer before terminating it.
  - This is a cleanup/stability change only; it does not weaken ACK proof checks and does not treat `ad_ack_c` as final ACK.
- Validation:
  - Build: `.\gradlew.bat --no-daemon :app:assembleDebug :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest` passed.
  - Actual UX comic+webtoon after reinstalling APKs:
    - Artifact: `build/ntk-ux-select/20260618_235710_actual_ux_after_quic_executor_grace`.
    - Result: `OK (2 tests)`, time `116.781s`.
    - Cronet executor rejection count: before `50`, after `0`.
    - Comic `/manhwa/36525/1807424`: first drawable `6964ms`, visible coverage `missingPx=0`, `placeholderPx=0`, strict ACK `/api/ad/ack` bridge submit `code=200`, proof `strictAdAck=true`.

  - Bad approach to avoid: do not suppress all errors; only explicit cancellation from superseded work is ignored.

- Root cause found:
  - `NtkWebViewFallbackManager.isStrictAdAckSuccessSource(...)` used broad substring checks: any source containing `ack-200` became strict.
  - Challenge-cookie sources such as `native-challenge-ad-ack-cookie-200`, `native-prepare-challenge-ad-ack-cookie-200`, `bridge-challenge-ad-ack-cookie-200`, and `captcha-bridge-challenge-ad-ack-cookie-200` therefore could be misclassified as strict ACK proof even though no `/api/ad/ack` 200 had happened.
  - `newtoki1.org` was also missing from the modern guard root predicate. That made `waitForNtkWebViewAckPreflightProof(...)` use the legacy join condition and repeatedly log `ntk_webview_ack_preflight_join_proof_hit` from a non-strict server ACK record instead of forcing the proof-capable ACK path.
- Accepted fixes:
  - Strict ACK source classification now rejects any `challenge` or `cookie` source and only accepts actual `/api/ad/ack` success source names such as `native-fetch-ack-200`, `native-ack-200`, `guard-bridge-ack-200`, `guard-fetch-ack-200`, and related bridge/fetch/state ACK sources.
  - `newtoki` roots are now treated like `sbxh` and `toonflix` in both `CustomHttpClient` and `NtkWebViewFallbackManager`, so modern roots require strict `/api/ad/ack` proof instead of legacy soft ACK.
  - Added a JVM test for source classification so challenge-cookie 200 cannot regress into strict proof again.
- Bad approaches / do not repeat:
  - Do not treat `ad_ack_c` from `/api/ad/challenge` as strict ACK success. It can be a useful scoped cookie/soft readiness signal, but it is not the requested actual `/api/ad/ack` 200 proof.
  - Do not trust `ntk_webview_ack_preflight_join_proof_hit` unless the root is in the modern guard set and `hasRecentStrictAdAckSuccess(...)` is true.
  - Do not rerun target ACK validation with the default `FirstDrawableMaxMs=3500` when comparing against the established 14000ms target budget; that caused a false first-drawable failure at `3593ms`.
  - JVM unit test execution in this Windows environment failed from a Gradle test executor/PATH encoding issue after compilation, not from the new assertion. Use instrumentation and compile output as the reliable fast check until that environment issue is fixed.
- Validation:

## 2026-06-20 00:20:00 +09:00 Random strict ACK passed but first drawable failed from stale generated URL

- New strict fresh random failure after `679fb177f`:
  - Path: `/webtoon/848103/1580934`
  - Mode: `native-ack`
  - Result: strict ACK succeeded, but first drawable did not arrive before the test window.
  - ACK proof was valid for the current path:
    - `bridge-ack-200`
    - `guard-fetch-ack-200`
    - `ntk_webview_ack_preflight_done ... success=true,ms=8097`
  - The failure was not an ACK failure.
- Root cause found in logs:
  - Initial generated URLs used stale image episode identity:
    - Wrong: `https://moamoabon.com/blacktoon/episodes/19192/688553/p001.jpg`
  - The later signed WebView/API image list was correct:
    - Correct: `https://moamoabon.com/black/episodes/19192/1580934/p001.jpg`
  - The correct p001 bytes were cached as the anchor asset, but the visible `PageRef.image` still pointed at the stale generated URL, so first drawable delivery kept following the wrong ref.
- Fix in progress:
  - When a verified non-generated API image list arrives, refresh existing generated seed refs even if this is a same-size or larger replacement.
  - Clear per-page failure/decode/delivery state during this generated-to-verified refresh.
  - For first-anchor generated 404 before first bitmap, retarget by page number to verified API/early/current image URLs before trying generated sibling reconstruction.
  - Keep the pre-first-bitmap early URL watcher alive long enough to catch late signed WebView/API lists after ACK proof; this does not delay opening the viewer, it only prevents the live page model from missing a better URL list that arrives after the initial generated seed failed.
  - Treat generated-to-non-generated same page URL changes as valid anchor replacements, not only generated-to-generated extension/path changes.
  - Do not shrink a full generated page model to a partial verified API subset. Partial verified p001/p002 replacements now merge into the existing full list by page number; full-size verified API lists can still replace the full list.
  - Same-size generated-to-verified URL refresh now mutates existing `PageRef` entries in place instead of clearing/re-adding the page list, so in-flight first-anchor decode is not invalidated by repeated late URL refreshes.
  - First-anchor decode now checks the cached anchor asset file before starting foreground stream/race. Logs showed p001 bytes were already cached, but stale foreground race 404 could still dominate the first drawable path.
  - URL replacement now also explicitly schedules cached-anchor urgent decode for the current page, so an already cached p001 can be posted as drawable without waiting for a stale foreground stream to fail.
  - The cached-anchor decode path is now separated from the generic visible-generated decode hedge so stale in-flight hedges cannot suppress the corrected anchor decode.
- Bad/risky approaches to avoid:
  - Do not treat this case as an ACK regression; ACK had actual scoped `/api/ad/ack` proof.
  - Do not increase first drawable timeout to hide the problem.
  - Do not keep relying on `ntkImageEpisodeId` generated URLs for every webtoon case when the signed API returns a different canonical image episode/path.
